title: RBI: Master Direction — Note Sorting Machines
applicability: Machines operated by banks, either directly by their staff or indirectly by their agents
description: RBI has issued a notification concerning Note Sorting Machines.
summary: The Reserve Bank of India has issued an updated Master Direction incorporating and updating extant guidelines on Note Sorting Machines, establishing comprehensive standards for note authentication, fitness sorting parameters, and machine calibration. This was issued to consolidate all current instructions on Note Sorting Machines at one place for reference and to update previous guidelines in the backdrop of new series banknotes and BIS standards. In practice, banks must ensure cash handling machines evaluate notes against specific criteria for soiling, limpness, tears, holes, stains, and repairs, test machines quarterly, and phase out discontinued NSM models by June 30, 2027.
takeaway: Ensure that Note Sorting Machines are tested for accuracy and consistency on a quarterly basis, maintain a signed certificate of testing for records, and phase out any discontinued NSM models on or before June 30, 2027.

title: RBI: Amendment — Reserve Bank of India (Local Area Banks - Acquisition and Holding of Shares or Voting Rights) Amendment Directions, 2026
applicability: Mutual funds registered with the Securities and Exchange Board of India, pension funds registered with the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority, and insurance companies registered with the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India that do not belong to the promoter group of the investee banking company, as well as portfolio managers and local area banks
description: RBI has issued a amendment concerning Reserve Bank of India (Local Area Banks - Acquisition and Holding of Shares or Voting Rights) Amendment Directions, 2026.
summary: The Reserve Bank of India has introduced the Reserve Bank of India (Local Area Banks - Acquisition and Holding of Shares or Voting Rights) Amendment Directions, 2026, which allow qualifying institutional investors such as mutual funds, pension funds, and insurance companies to obtain one-time approval for subsequent acquisitions of major shareholding up to 10 percent of the paid-up share capital or voting rights of a banking company. This was decided based on a review to streamline the prior approval process for specific institutional investors while maintaining regulatory oversight. In practice, qualifying persons must now submit applications through PRAVAAH along with Form A, banking companies must furnish comments in Form A1, and major shareholders or qualifying persons with one-time approval must report any decrease or increase of aggregate holding to below or above five percent within three working days.
takeaway: Submit applications for one-time approval through PRAVAAH along with Form A, ensure the concerned banking company furnishes its comments in Form A1, and report any decrease or increase of aggregate holding to below or above five percent to the Reserve Bank and the concerned banking company within three working days of such an event.

summary: The Reserve Bank of India has introduced the Reserve Bank of India (Payments Banks - Acquisition and Holding of Shares or Voting Rights) Amendment Directions, 2026, which modify the Master Direction of November 28, 2025. This amendment allows qualifying entities such as mutual funds, insurance companies, and pension funds to apply for a one-time approval through PRAVAAH for subsequent acquisitions of major shareholding up to 10 percent. The Reserve Bank issued these directions based on a review to streamline shareholding acquisition rules while maintaining regulatory oversight and fit-and-proper criteria. In practice, qualifying entities must submit applications via PRAVAAH with Form A, banking companies must furnish comments in Form A1, and approved entities must report changes in aggregate holdings crossing five percent within three working days.
takeaway: Submit applications for one-time approval through the PRAVAAH portal along with Form A, and report any decrease or increase of aggregate holding below or above five percent to the Reserve Bank and the concerned banking company within three working days.

summary: This circular commences the levy of a fee for delayed filing of forms under Regulation 47B of the Liquidation Process Regulations. description: IBBI has issued a circular concerning further extension of time for filing electronic forms to monitor insolvency resolution processes for Personal Guarantors to Corporate Debtors.
summary: The Board has further extended the deadline for filing electronic forms PGIRP-1 to PGIRP-6 for monitoring insolvency resolution processes concerning personal guarantors to corporate debtors. This extension was issued in response to feedback received from Insolvency Professionals and Insolvency Professional Agencies seeking more time due to practical difficulties. In practice, compliance workflows are adjusted such that penalties for delayed submission or modification of these forms will now be levied only after the new deadline.
takeaway: Update internal filing schedules to submit all applicable PGIRP-1 to PGIRP-6 forms by the extended deadline of 31st December 2026, noting that penalties for delayed submission or modification will only be levied after this date.

title: IBBI: Circular — Judgments of the Hon'ble Bombay High Court and Delhi High Court on cessation of interim moratorium in respect of personal guarantors to corporate debtors
applicability: All Registered Insolvency Professionals, All Recognised Insolvency Professional Entities, and All Registered Insolvency Professional Agencies in respect of personal guarantors to corporate debtors
description: IBBI has issued a circular concerning Judgments of the Hon'ble Bombay High Court and Delhi High Court on cessation of interim moratorium in respect of personal guarantors to corporate debtors.
summary: The IBBI clarified the application of sub-section (4) of sections 96 and 124 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, following judgments by the Bombay and Delhi High Courts regarding personal guarantors to corporate debtors. The regulator issued this circular to address the legal position on whether interim moratoriums cease for applications pending before the Adjudicating Authority as of the effective date. In practice, compliance workflows involving personal guarantor insolvency proceedings must account for the cessation of interim moratoriums effective from May 26, 2026, for both pending and new applications.
takeaway: Review active insolvency proceedings involving personal guarantors to corporate debtors to confirm that interim moratoriums have ceased to operate as of May 26, 2026, in accordance with the judgments and the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (Amendment) Act, 2026.

description: CIRCULAR
Subject: Judgments of the Hon'ble Bombay High Court and Delhi High Court on cessation of interim moratorium in respect of personal guarantors to corporate debtors.
summary:
The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (Amendment) Act, 2026 inserted sub-section (4) in 
sections 96 and 124 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, providing that the interim 
moratorium shall not apply in respect of a personal guarantor to a corporate debtor, with effect 
from 26th May, 2026.

Subject: Judgments of the Hon'ble Bombay High Court and Delhi High Court on 
cessation of interim moratorium in respect of personal guarantors to corporate debtors.

Accordingly, it may be noted that the interim moratorium under section 96 (and, 
correspondingly, section 124) of the Code, in respect of a personal guarantor to a corporate 
debtor, has ceased to operate with effect from 26th May, 2026 in respect of applications pending 
before Adjudicating Authority as on that date.
takeaway:
Accordingly, it may be noted that the interim moratorium under section 96 (and, 
correspondingly, section 124) of the Code, in respect of a personal guarantor to a corporate 
debtor, has ceased to operate with effect from 26th May, 2026 in respect of applications pending 
before Adjudicating Authority as on that date.
